title: What are crystal skulls?
summary: A republished 'lost' episode on crystal skulls. Hosts open by explaining it was recorded earlier and forgotten, then cover a news story about a crystal skull found in a Bavarian attic that belonged to a woman married to an SS officer and was linked to Heinrich Himmler. They explain the 2012 Mayan thirteen-skull legend, then examine the Mitchell-Hedges skull and its questionable backstory (Anna Mitchell-Hedges, F.A. Mitchell-Hedges, Sydney Bernie, Sotheby's), the British Museum skull, Paris skull, Smithsonian skull, and other skulls. They discuss piezoelectricity and healing claims, Frank Dorland's study and the Hewlett-Packard claim, Brazilian crystal and 1800s German origins, Eugene Boban, the British Museum and Jane Walsh's 2005 Smithsonian analysis showing modern tool marks, and pop culture references. The episode ends with a listener mail segment about the Daily Pep Talk website and a sponsor read for Lynda.com.
topics: Indiana Jones Kingdom of the Crystal Skull

entities.name: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull

segments.title: Lost episode intro
segments.summary: Hosts explain this is a long-lost episode recorded earlier and published late, with a caveat that some information is dated.

segments.title: News: crystal skull found in Bavarian attic
segments.summary: A crystal skull was reportedly found hidden in an attic in a Bavarian house, linked to a woman married to an SS officer and said to have belonged to Heinrich Himmler. Swiss journalist Luke Bergen claims it is Mayan, and the hosts doubt the claim. The hosts also mention Nazi archaeology programs.

segments.title: Mayan thirteen-skull legend and 2012
segments.summary: The hosts describe the legend that thirteen Mayan crystal skulls must be reunited before a December 21 deadline or the world ends. They note far more than thirteen skulls exist, which raises doubts about authenticity.

segments.title: Overview of crystal skulls and their claimed powers
segments.summary: Crystal skulls vary in size, detail, clarity and color. Some people link them to Mayans or Atlantis, and they are rumored to heal, provide visions, make sounds, and offer enlightenment.

segments.title: Mitchell-Hedges skull and Anna's story
segments.summary: The Mitchell-Hedges skull is described as the most famous, a clear life-size crystal skull with a detachable jaw. Anna Mitchell-Hedges said she found it at Lubaantun near Belize on her seventeenth birthday, and claimed it was used for transferring priestly knowledge. The hosts point out inconsistencies in her account.

segments.title: Provenance problems and later owners of the Mitchell-Hedges skull
segments.summary: Documented history shows the skull was owned by Sydney Bernie, auctioned and bought back from Sotheby's. F.A. Mitchell-Hedges's 1954 book mentions it only once and he alleged it was carved by rubbing sand over 150 years. Bill Hollman now owns it and plans a Sedona museum.
topics: F.A. Mitchell-Hedges book Danger My Ally

segments.title: Other famous skulls and museum examinations
segments.summary: The hosts cover the British Museum skull, the Paris skull at the Musée de l'Homme, the anonymous hollow Smithsonian skull, and collectors' skulls such as Max, Amy, and Shanna Ra. Eugene Boban, a French dealer in Mayan relics, is linked to several. Brazilian crystal and 1800s German carving are suggested.

segments.title: Piezoelectricity, Dorland tests, and fraud evidence
segments.summary: Hosts explain quartz piezoelectricity as a basis for healing claims. Frank Dorland's claims of visions and a Hewlett-Packard test are described and questioned. Jane Walsh's 2005 electron microscope analysis found modern tool marks, and the British Museum concluded the skulls were made with European tools in the 1800s.

segments.title: Pop culture references
segments.summary: The hosts list crystal skull references in Stargate SG-1, Nancy Drew games, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull, which they criticize.
topics: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
